questions.prompt: In science, a pure substance is…
options: a substance made of only one kind of particle

feedback.0: That's the everyday (shopping) meaning. The scientific meaning is about particles.

questions.explain: A pure substance contains only one kind of particle, like distilled water, gold or table salt.

questions.prompt: Sort into pure substances and mixtures.
questions.hint: Ask: does it contain only ONE kind of particle?
questions.explain: Gold, distilled water, salt and oxygen each contain only one kind of particle. Milk, air, sea water and soil contain several substances.

questions.prompt: Sort these mixtures into homogeneous and heterogeneous.
questions.explain: Homogeneous mixtures look the same everywhere (solutions and alloys). Heterogeneous ones have parts you can see or that separate out.

questions.prompt: Brass looks like one shiny metal. Why is it a mixture?
options: It contains copper and zinc atoms mixed but not chemically joined
It is made in a factory
questions.explain: Brass is an alloy: a mixture of copper and zinc. The proportions can vary.

questions.prompt: A clear liquid boils over a range from 101 °C to 104 °C. What can you conclude?
options: It is a mixture (for example, salt water)
It is a pure substance that isn't water
questions.hint: Pure substances boil at ONE exact temperature.
questions.explain: Boiling over a range, and above 100 °C, shows impurities are present, so it's a mixture such as salt water.

questions.prompt: Which statements about MIXTURES are true? Choose all that apply.
options: The substances keep their own properties
The amounts of each substance can vary
They can be separated by physical methods
questions.explain: In a mixture, substances are not chemically joined; they keep their properties, can be in any proportion, and can be physically separated. Homogeneous mixtures don't look mixed.

questions.text: A pure substance melts at one ___ temperature. A mixture that looks the same everywhere is called ___.
questions.explain: Pure substances have sharp melting and boiling points. Uniform mixtures are homogeneous.

questions.prompt: Why do people in cold countries spread salt on icy roads?
options: Salt water freezes below 0 °C, so the ice melts
Salt reacts with ice to make heat
questions.explain: Impurities lower the freezing point. Salt water freezes at a lower temperature than pure water, so ice melts even when it's a bit below 0 °C.

questions.prompt: Match each example to what it is.
questions.explain: Distilled water has one kind of particle; nimbu pani looks uniform; muddy water has visible bits.

questions.prompt: A ghee packet says 'Pure Desi Ghee'. Explain what 'pure' means here and why a scientist might disagree.
questions.modelAnswer: On the label, 'pure' means nothing else (like vegetable oil) has been added to the ghee. A scientist would say ghee is not a pure substance, because it is a mixture of many different fats and other substances, not one kind of particle.
rubric: I explained the everyday meaning (nothing added / not adulterated)
I said ghee contains several different substances
I used the idea of one kind of particle for a pure substance
questions.explain: Everyday 'pure' = unadulterated; scientific 'pure' = one kind of particle.
